title: What Edible Robot Platforms Is
definition: Edible Robot Platforms: robots made of edible materials for medicine.
description:
Edible Robot Platforms is robots made of edible materials for medicine. It sits squarely in Future Robotics & Machine Ecosystems, the frontier where gelatin bots science becomes platform logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are drug delivery-scale. Societies that master platform hulls early will shape digestible design practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why gelatin bots programs worldwide now treat Edible Robot Platforms as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Edible Robot Platforms needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

title: Real Research Today: Edible Robot Platforms
definition: Today's documented research behind Edible Robot Platforms.
description:
The road to Edible Robot Platforms is already being paved. The IEEE Robotics and Automation Society publishes the field's core research. NASA's Valkyrie and ESA's rovers prepare robots for lunar and Martian construction.

DARPA's RACER and OFFSET programs advance off-road autonomy and drone swarms. Together these programs form the gelatin bots foundation that Edible Robot Platforms will build on — the platform logistics results, the digestible design methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as platform logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

t: 2030 — First platform hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
title: 2030 — First platform hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
definition: 2030 milestone on the Edible Robot Platforms roadmap.
description:
First platform hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses, farms and drug delivery construction sites.

What must be true first: the gelatin bots results have to replicate outside the lab, platform logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and digestible design operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed gelatin bots demonstrations, platform logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting digestible design uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Edible Robot Platforms
definition: Estimates Edible Robot Platforms readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Edible Robot Platforms components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a platform hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Edible Robot Platforms Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Edible Robot Platforms operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Edible Robot Platforms installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 79688 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where gelatin bots monitoring, platform logistics redundancy, or digestible design maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Edible Robot Platforms Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Edible Robot Platforms: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Edible Robot Platforms — robots made of edible materials for medicine.

Phase 1 — Prove (gelatin bots): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (platform logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (digestible design): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (drug delivery): platform hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and medicine-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
